full_judgment: 2. Short facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that the above named petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 219 of 1991 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge (Sadar), Comilla for declaration of their title in the suit land measuring an area of .64 acres out of 129 acres of land under CS Plot Nos. 511 and 512 and CS Khatian No. 97. Defendant Nos.1-2, 3-5 and 16-19 contested the suit by filing 3(three) sets of written statements denying all the material allegations of the plaint and contended that the plaintiffs have no right, title and possession in the suit land and also pointed out certain formal defects, namely, the description of the suit properties was wrong, vague and indefinite, the suit was barred by limitation and the suit was not also maintainable in its present form. At the trial both the parties examined oral and documentary evidences in support of their respective claims. The trial Court on consideration of the materials and evidence on record was pleased to dismiss the suit on merit. Against which the plaintiffs as appellants preferred Title Appeal No. 261 of 1996 before the learned District Judge, Comilla which was ultimately transmitted to the Court of learned Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla for disposal and during pendency of the appeal, the plaintiff-appellants engaged a Senior Advocate to conduct the appeal, who on going through the case record advised the plaintiff-appellants (hereinafter called "the plaintiff-petitioner") to withdraw the appeal as well as suit and to institute a partition suit, since the defendants also claimed right, title and possession in the suit land on the basis of a registered document. Therefore, plaintiff-petitioners filed a petition under Order XXIII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter called the Code) before the learned Subordinate Judge, Comilla for withdrawal of the suit with the permission to sue afresh on the ground of formal defect. The learned Subordinate Judge upon hearing the parties at length was pleased to disallow the prayer for withdrawal of the suit with permission to sue afresh by his order dated 14-1-98.
